I also plan to draft a sentence on hypersensitivity, highlighting rare cases and the need for immediate discontinuation. It’s important to instruct patients to stop the medication and seek medical care if these arise. rounds.response:
HCP label — Hepatic: "Elevations of liver enzymes (ALT, AST) were observed in the phase 3 program; these abnormalities were generally asymptomatic and reversible on interruption of therapy, and no Hy’s law cases were observed. Obtain baseline liver tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin), repeat at approximately 2–4 weeks after treatment initiation, and thereafter periodically as clinically indicated. Interrupt therapy if ALT or AST ≥3×ULN in the presence of symptoms of liver injury, or ≥5×ULN without symptoms; discontinue therapy if ALT or AST ≥8×ULN or if jaundice or other signs of clinically significant liver injury occur." 

HCP label — Hypersensitivity: "Rare but serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported; if signs of hypersensitivity (for example, urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm, or hypotension) occur, stop the drug immediately and initiate appropriate emergency treatment. Do not rechallenge patients who have experienced a severe hypersensitivity reaction."

Limitations of Use / Cross‑references: "Limitations of Use: Efficacy has not been established in patients with severe renal impairment; use is not recommended in this population. (See Use in Specific Populations and Dosage and Administration—no dosing recommendations can be provided for patients with severe renal impairment.)"

Patient leaflet — liver counseling (plain language): "Before you start, you will have a blood test to check your liver; you should have another test about 2–4 weeks after starting and more tests as your doctor thinks necessary. Stop taking the medicine and call your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, very dark urine, or severe or ongoing nausea or vomiting."

Patient leaflet — hypersensitivity/action (plain language): "Stop the medicine and get urgent medical help right away if you develop a rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, trouble breathing, or fainting; do not take this medicine again if you had a severe allergic reaction unless your doctor tells you to."
